349:   public void onStart() {
350:     super.onStart();
351: 
352:     if (jsBridgeClassName != null) {
353:       tryLoadingJsBridge(jsBridgeClassName);
354:     }
355: 
356:     // Due to the way Android initializes instrumentation - all instrumentations have the
357:     // possibility of seeing the Application and its classes in an inconsistent state.
358:     // Specifically ActivityThread creates Instrumentation first, initializes it, and calls
359:     // instrumentation.onCreate(). After it does that, it calls
360:     // instrumentation.callApplicationOnCreate() which ends up calling the application's
361:     // onCreateMethod.
362:     //
363:     // So, Android's InstrumentationTestRunner's onCreate method() spawns a separate thread to
364:     // execute tests. This causes tests to start accessing the application and its classes while
365:     // the ActivityThread is calling callApplicationOnCreate() in its own thread.
366:     //
367:     // This makes it possible for tests to see the application in a state that is normally never
368:     // visible: pre-application.onCreate() and during application.onCreate()).
369:     //
370:     // *phew* that sucks! Here we waitForOnIdleSync() to ensure onCreate has completed before we
371:     // start executing tests.
372:     waitForIdleSync();
373: 
374:     // If the user has not yet set up a ContextClassLoader, they may need one set up for them
375:     // now.  They cannot see the one we set up in onCreate() because that took place on a
376:     // different thread.
377:     setupDexmakerClassloader();
378: 
379:     InstrumentationConnection.getInstance().init(this, new ActivityFinisher());
